items.title: Gene's Rule: can you tell a good team by how it answers?
items.finding: Gene's rule: a good team scores right back after the other side scores. Across NFL drives since 1999, MLB half-innings since 1977 and NHL goals since 2015, teams score right after being scored on at the same rate they score any other time (NFL 33 vs 34 per 100). Teams that answer more do win more, but answering better than you usually score predicts nothing and does not repeat from year to year. Gene teams are good teams because answering is scoring. Piece queued. Follow-up (the Rangers point): teams good on the power play are barely more likely than chance to be good on the penalty kill too (13 vs 11 of 100 team-seasons), and answering teams' better special teams come from being better teams. The 2023-24 Rangers really were top 3 in both.

items.title: What do hitting stats actually measure?
items.finding: Factor-analyzing every hitter from 2021 to 2025 turns up four or five underlying traits: patience, contact, speed and power, maybe launch angle. Speed is the cleanest. Contact and power may be one trade-off, not two traits. The best model only fits moderately on a fresh sample (CFI .91, RMSEA .12), so this is not a result yet.

items.title: Is it the player or the season?
items.finding: Ranking each stat within its own season fixes era: 109 RBI in 1968 was as rare as 132 in 2025. It does not make the stats more stable from year to year, and it does not fix the factor models within one era. It helps them modestly across eras (CFI .85 to .89). The same lookup now covers pitchers (ranked only against their own job) and every NFL player since 1999 (ranked within position).

items.title: Yards per play, adjusted for who you played
items.finding: Calling each week's winners from the weeks before it, schedule-adjusted yards per play picked 234 of 359 college games and 62 of 93 NFL games. Points did about as well. So it is a good read, not a better one, and it gets graded on the game cards every week.

items.title: When is a basketball lead safe?
items.finding: Across last season, a 1-to-3-point halftime lead won 51 of 100 NBA games and 62 of 100 men's college games. A college lead also hints at which team is better. The numbers come from one source so far, and nothing goes on a card until a second source agrees.
